problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-\frac{7}{3x}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Graphing a Stretched Negative Reciprocal Function
examples.worked_solution:
To plot $y = -\dfrac{1}{5x},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\dfrac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/d5d93e12275c683e0a56f0ec9a0c99540a7774879cd0f8fa69151ddba68a44fa.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $\dfrac 1 5$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\dfrac{1}{5x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/30ace3126ec127b9949ebf599d615020b9770458825d22460e9e7e0b3d5efec3.png)

feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2x}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot $y=\frac{1}{2x},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=\frac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/a32495fcca947d01cf8d3218fc5cfc0cce083a34e6fb6b629d92ba9e47039a6e.png)

- Stretch the result by a scale factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=\frac{1}{2x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/f3a1cac41b2f9d6773226d76722508e6d7f368a42a0f7e86a5d8407d6f42c149.png)
